findings.pdf_says: Figure E.4 — COBOL communication environment: a drawn diagram with four columns (COBOL Program box listing RECEIVE, RECEIVE, SEND, ..SEND, .....RECEIVE, SEND; a vertical 'Communication Descriptions (CD)' bar labelled 'COBOL/MCS Interface'; the Message Control System (MCS) with an 'Input Queues' box and an 'Output Queues' box, '(communication using queues)' and '(transaction communication)'; a vertical 'ENABLE / DISABLE' bar labelled 'MCS/Communication Device Interface'; and five Communication Devices), with arrows showing data flowing devices -> input queues -> RECEIVE, SEND -> output queues -> devices, and the transaction-communication RECEIVE/SEND paths bypassing the queues.

findings.why_it_matters: The figure was OCR'd into fragmentary tables: the arrows (all of the data-flow information), the device column and the CD and ENABLE/DISABLE bars are lost or scrambled ('Communication' and 'Descriptions' split into separate cells, 'ENABLE' duplicated, 'DISABLE' detached). The informative text on page 757 points the reader to this figure for the relationships among RECEIVE/SEND, the MCS queues and ENABLE/DISABLE; the markdown cannot convey them. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is lost.

findings.pdf_says: Figure E.5 — Hierarchy of queues: a tree with levels QUEUE (A), SUB-QUEUE (1) (B, C), SUB-QUEUE (2) (D, E under B; F, G under C), SUB-QUEUE (3) (H, I under D; J, K under E; L, M under F; N, O under G) and MESSAGE (H: Z1 X2; I: X3 X4 X5; J: X1 Y3 Y5 Z5; K: Z6 Z7 Y6; L: Y7 Y8; M: Y1 Y2; N: X6; O: Z2 Z3 Z4 Y4).
findings.why_it_matters: The tree structure is lost: the SUB-QUEUE (3) level label and sub-queue-3 names H, J, K, L, M and N are missing, the parent/child edges are gone, and 'MESSAGE' displaced X2's column so the message lists no longer line up under their sub-queues. The worked examples on page 762 (e.g. Sub-queue-3 N returns Message X6; Queue A returns Z1) cannot be followed from the markdown. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is lost.
